english.title: Distribute other than in course of business a device / product / component so that it prejudicially affects the owner
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) otherwise than in the course of a business, distributed to such an extent as to affect prejudicially the copyright owner, a

(A)_[device,]_
(B)_[product,]_
(C)_[component,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY THE DEVICE / PRODUCT / COMPONENT..), which was primarily designed, produced or adapted for the purpose of enabling or facilitating the circumvention of effective technological measures
english.legislation: Contrary to section 296ZB(1)(d) and (4) of the Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: It is not enough that the technological measure is a discouragement or general commercial hindrance to copyright infringement, it must be a measure which physically prevents it. (R v Higgs 2008) EWCA Crim 1324 [2009] and 1 WLR 73, [2008].

other.penalty:
Summary: Three months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time Limit on Prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
